summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of pseudotumor cerebri and a VP shunt, previously repositioned for right lower quadrant pain, was readmitted due to recurrent sharp RLQ pain and nausea. Initial evaluation showed no evidence of infection, obstruction, or shunt displacement. Surgical consultation found no indication for intervention. Pain was managed with transition from short-acting opioids to scheduled OxyContin, resulting in improved control. Chronic conditions including diabetes, hypertension, depression, migraines, and obstructive sleep apnea were monitored. The patient was discharged home with a pain management plan, follow-up arranged with primary care and pain specialists, and recommendations to restart and re-evaluate CPAP therapy due to narcotic use.
